title: Build Claude Agent Teams Like a Pro

slides.text:
Most people use Claude Code as a <accent>single agent</accent>.

But there's an experimental feature that lets you spin up <accent>multiple agents</accent> that work in parallel, talk to each other, and QA each other's work.

Here's the framework to do it right.

slides.heading: Sub-agents vs <accent>Agent Teams</accent>
before: Report back to one main agent

slides.heading: Step 1: <accent>Enable</accent> the Feature
slides.body:
Agent Teams are experimental.
Disabled by default.
One setting turns it on.

slides.heading: Step 2: <accent>Prompt</accent> with Structure
slides.caption: Name the agents. Define roles. Assign file ownership. Set deliverables.

slides.heading: Step 3: Watch Them <accent>Build</accent>
slides.caption: Each agent gets its own context window. They coordinate via shared tasks and messaging.

slides.heading: The <accent>Do vs Don't</accent> Rules
slides.caption: Follow these prompting rules to avoid the #1 failure mode: agents overwriting each other.

slides.heading: The <accent>QA Loop</accent> Pattern
items: Spawn dev agents for parallel work (frontend, backend, etc.)
Add a dedicated QA agent that reviews others' work
QA finds issues and sends them back to dev agents
Automated review cycle without human intervention
Monitor via tmux split-pane to watch all agents live

slides.heading: When <accent>NOT</accent> to Use Teams
slides.body:
- Simple tasks that one agent can handle
- Sequential work where each step depends on the last
- Same-file edits (agents will overwrite each other)
- When sub-agents are good enough

Teams shine for parallel, multi-domain projects.

slides.text:
The future of AI coding isn't one agent doing everything.
It's a team of agents, each owning their domain,
coordinating like real developers.
